messages:
drew: heads up — noticed weird state in console: roles listed for a handful of tenants that report no effective privileges. looks like 'ghost roles' after a scope migration. reproducible on staging :frowning:
mari: hmm. any steps to repro? or a tenant id we can poke? :eyes:
drew: repro: create role -> bind to service-account -> run scope-migration job -> UI shows binding but effective privileges empty. API returns empty list for /v1/effective-privs until you re-save the binding. suspect event ordering between authz-service and scope-indexer.
alex: can you paste the raw API responses? do we get an empty array or a 500?
drew: raw: `GET /v1/effective-privs?principal=svc-123&tenant=acme` -> `{"privileges":[]}`
       while `GET /v1/role-bindings?principal=svc-123` returns the binding object. UI is just reflecting the empty effective-privs.
sophie: that smells like eventual-consistency. indexer probably processes migration events after authz writes, and our console relies on effective-privs read path for display.
mari: two possible fixes: 1) console shows role-bindings and a 'calculated' preview immediately (derive from binding + current roles) so we don't show empty; 2) ensure scope-indexer emits an immediate recompute event synchronously on migration.
alex: option 1 is lowest-risk UX patch. we can compute an optimistic effective-priv view in the client using role definitions and bindings (both available from API).
sophie: agree. fallback: show a soft-warning "computing effective privileges" with a CTA to refresh. avoids false-empty state.
drew: for longer term we should make the indexer emit a tombstone/flush event so dashboard reads are consistent. but that needs infra and careful rollout.
mari: telemetry questions: how many users/tenants hit this? can we add a metered event when UI observes binding but no effective-privs? that would help prioritize.
ops-bot: deploy scheduled: canary console change going out at 22:00 UTC — config flag `ui.optimistic_effective_privs=true`.
alex: quick API-work idea: `POST /v1/effective-privs/refresh?principal=...` — small endpoint to trigger recompute for a principal. console could call it on first open if it sees empty.
sophie: slight caution: rate-limit that endpoint and require tenant-admin. we don't want mass-trigger storms during a migration.
drew: plan proposal: 1) ship console optimistic derivation + soft-warning (canary tonight) 2) add telemetry event for ghost-role sightings 3) implement rate-limited recompute endpoint for manual refresh 4) scope-indexer followup to guarantee ordering (longer ticket)
mari: OK. assign owners: alex -> console UI patch + telemetry; sophie -> recompute endpoint + rate-limits; drew -> followup ticket for indexer ordering and migration preflight; i'll own rollout coordination and canary monitor.
alex: I'll open PR with demo screenshots and a simple algorithm: merge bindings + static role rules -> show inferred privileges. fallback to real effective-privs when available.
sophie: I'll add an auth check and a per-tenant token on the recompute endpoint, and a background dedupe queue.
ops-bot: canary monitor: will track `ghost-role.sighting` metric, alert if rate > 5/min over 5m during rollout.
drew: thanks team. one more UX note: show a tiny tooltip explaining why computed vs authoritative may differ. reduces support tickets.
mari: agreed. i'll update release notes and ping support with a short blurb.
